title: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision (MPM Mar 17-18, 2027 — no Outlook Report)
source: NEWS: boj.or.jp 'Monetary Policy Meetings' schedule page (en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 41,959 bytes) and column-parsed out of the HTML by this session independently of the fetch that seeded the three 2026 BoJ entries. The page carries two tables; the 'Table : 2027' row parses as ['Mar. 17 (Wed.), 18 (Thurs.)', '-', 'Mar. 29 (Mon.)', 'May 7 (Fri.)'] against the header 'Date of MPM | Outlook Report (The Bank's View) | Summary of Opinions | MPM Minutes'. The '-' is the primary evidence that this is NOT an Outlook Report meeting. The decision publishes at the meeting's conclusion on the second day. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the four sibling BoJ entries: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: and no slot for any other central bank, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and a schedule published ~18 months ahead is the most movable kind
notes: Proposed during the boj-decision-2027-01-22 initial research (2026-09-05) because that ledger's branch structure needs the venue immediately after January and could not name it from the calendar. SAME CHANNEL, SAME CAVEAT AS THE FOUR OTHER BoJ ENTRIES: a BoJ move propagates to this calendar's long-duration AI names through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order for a US equity book and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers; symbols is empty and no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed. TWO FACTS THAT MAKE THIS VENUE DISTINCTIVE, both from primary tables parsed 2026-09-05. (1) It is the WORST-INFORMED 2027 meeting on Japanese CPI: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html puts the February-2027 national CPI on 2027-03-19, ONE DAY AFTER this meeting concludes, so the board decides on January data (released 2027-02-19) while the February print sits one day out of reach — the exact inverse of boj-decision-2027-01-22, which meets ON its CPI release date. (2) It is the BEST-informed 2027 meeting on wages: Rengo's shunto first tally has landed mid-March in recent cycles (2026: demand 5.94% reported 2026-03-02, result 5.26% reported 2026-03-23, per Japan Times / Rengo), so this is the first MPM of the year that can cite spring wage momentum rather than forecast it. Those two facts pull in opposite directions and are why the January ledger treats March as a genuine alternative venue rather than a fallback. Policy rate was 1.0% as of the 2026-07-31 statement (8-1, Takata dissenting for 1.25%); anything above that at this date came from the 2026 H2 sequence or from January.
